featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

Our very first experience at this restaurant started with a big "NO" from the staff.

As a family visiting with a toddler, I requested a toddler/high chair. I was informed that they did not have any. I then requested a stack chair or any alternative seating arrangement that could help accommodate my child, but that request was also declined. I was told that the available chairs were reserved only for adults waiting outside.

I approached the cashier and politely asked why a family restaurant had not considered seating arrangements for children or toddlers. To my surprise, the response was extremely rude. I was told, "We only cater to adults. We do not bother about kids' seating arrangements. It's your problem, and you'll have to deal with it. We can't help you."

This level of customer service was disappointing and unacceptable. A family restaurant should be more considerate and accommodating towards families with young children.

Unfortunately, the experience did not improve thereafter. The food was highly overpriced for the quality and overall experience offered and did not justify the premium pricing.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this place to families with young children. Hospitality begins with attitude, and sadly, that was missing here.

Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: VISHAL UPADHYAY
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered cheese pav bhaji, and masala dosa and both were extremely delicious. We loved both the items. Cost wise it appeared a little costly given the ambience, and quality of service. It was situated near Dadar railway station and is fine for some snacking.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

featured_reviews.name: imran khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is located very near to Dadar East railway station... AC dining room. But the space is very small. Outdoor sitting area is spacious but one cannot sit there during daytime.
Food was amazing tasty. A little higher price.. people may feel for this .. however if you compare to food outlets in the mall .. it's the same. Combos one can have .. quantity fulfills  the hunger for one person. Overall nice experience. Recommended if around Dadar railway station.

featured_reviews.name: Taran Arora
featured_reviews.review_text: If you enjoy South Indian food and want a cleaner, more café-style experience in Dadar, Mutuswami is worth trying. Best dishes to order are Benne dosa, thatte idli, rasam rice , filter coffee and pineapple sheera.  Staff is very courteous and welcoming.

featured_reviews.name: Mithil Thakker
featured_reviews.review_text:
This one has become our most favourite go to place whenever close to Dadar East Station.

They have indoor and outdoor seating. Post 8 pm it's a busy schedule for the restaurant so go a bit early to get the best available table of the house.

Our food recommendations.

Podi Idli:
You have to visit this place to experience this extraordinary delicacy of the house .

Benne Masala Dosa:
This one won't disappoint you if you are fond of benne then definitely give this a try.

Pav Bhaji:
Again a house supremacy. Spicy and Tangy burst of flavours with every bite .

The Mango Milkshake was rich and thick  . Even their cold coffee has a supreme vibe.

Pineapple Sheera .
When at a South Indian cuisine specialist restaurant then you can't miss this legendary dish . Indeed a heavenly experience.

Overall a delightful experience as always.

Happy and Safe Fooding Until Next Time.

featured_reviews.review_text: I have been an Anand Bhavan evangelist but the new owner is rude and arrogant brat. They have best sambar, rasam, and their special masala dosa is out of the world. However, with Iran war, they have started charging for extra sambhar/chutney. No worries, it is understandable but the young dude at the counter straight up lied saying they have always been charging extra (I have been visiting for more than a decade and was never charged). More importantly, the young dude went on a monologue of how Indians don't deserve free stuff and is super rude and arrogant. While his fathers who ran the restaurant are kind, his arrogance will be the downfall of this gem of Matunga. Good luck Mr Sourdough baker, keep feeding your lies to yourself.

featured_reviews.name: Nitheesh K S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food was definitely good (4/5) — well prepared and tasty. However, the service was average (3/5) and didn’t really match the quality of the food.

The biggest concern was staff behaviour (1/5). The staff at the counter were quite controlling about seating — we were asked to sit with other families even when multiple tables were vacant. It felt uncomfortable and lacked basic privacy.

Also, they do not accept digital payments, which can be inconvenient.

The elderly person at the counter was particularly rude. In just about 20 minutes, I saw him argue with at least three different customers. The attitude came across as dismissive and unwelcoming.

Overall, decent food, but the experience is significantly affected by poor staff behaviour. Would recommend only if you want to experience being controlled and dictated, after paying money from your pocket.

featured_reviews.name: vishal mahasukh joshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very cozy old Mumbai character place for authentic south indian food. For me the "feast" started with single idli vada dip in piping hot sambar with fresh coconut chutney. Followed by crisp golden roasted Rava masala dosa. I asked for the masla (alu sabji) seperately to maintain the crispness of the dosa till last bite. Again served with sambar, tomato chutney and coconut chutney...the version of dessert here was a first time experience for me here. A slice of bread with neatly trimmed edges, golden roasted in sumptuous butter and sprinkled with brown sugar ... Perfect blend of bit salty and sweet taste with those sugar granules bursting and dissolving in your mouth when they are partially warm. That was an indulging experience...and you think it's over?
Coffee served in small "pyali and katori" to close the perfect deal...
Overall one of the best lunch I had in a company of a very good friend, who introduced me to this place at the first instance.
All served with a smile on face.
If in this part of Mumbai, don't miss the opportunity.

featured_reviews.name: chirag shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Authentic South Indian Taste in the Heart of Matunga!

Udipi in Matunga truly stands out for serving one of the most authentic South Indian meals in the area. The food tastes homely, fresh, and full of flavour — from the perfectly crisp dosas to the soft idlis and that classic filter coffee which completes the meal beautifully.

What makes it even better is that the entire restaurant is fully air-conditioned, making dining here a pleasant experience even on hot days. The place is clean, well-maintained, and comfortable for families as well as groups of friends.

The service is quick, polite, and efficient — exactly what you’d expect from a traditional Udipi restaurant.

If you’re looking for genuine South Indian food in Matunga that combines great taste, comfort, and a welcoming vibe, this is definitely one of the best spots to visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Anchal Garg
featured_reviews.review_text:
A decent restaurant to try some authentic South Indian food 🥘 at a reasonable price.
Firstly, we had to wait for our turn so we waited in the queue for 15-20 minutes. Their service is lil slow as they took sometime to prepare the dosas but the taste was not compromised.
The dosas were crisp and the sambhar tasted good. Not too spicy and the appropriate amount of sourness.
It was on my bucket list to cover all the famous South Indian joints in Matunga, and it one is well covered. A must try for the crispy dosas and filter coffee ☕️

featured_reviews.name: Arvind Nadkarni
featured_reviews.review_text: Legendary & Authentic, no-frills Manglorean/konkani menu. Well prepared & served. Takes some waiting during peak hours(lunch & dinner time). featured_reviews.review_text: We went on Sunday Afternoon and it was full pack But waiting time 10-15 minutes only. Service was quick and food was excellent taste was excellent, polite staff. Recommended to all for best south indian food.

featured_reviews.name: ATS
featured_reviews.review_text:
An iconic South Indian cuisine restaurant in the iconic Matunga east neighbourhood of Mumbai. Everything, I repeat, every damn food item here is par excellence.

Things eaten: Paniyaram, Rassam, Medu Vada, Kanchipuram idli, appam with coconut stew, mysore onion dosa, cheese pav bhaji, pineapple sheera AND filter coffee.

Verdict: The Medu vada is truly one of the best I have ever had. It is so soft yet crispy at the same time. The coconut chutney and Tamilian sambar is unparalleled. Appam with coconut stew is amazing as well. Especially the stew was so delicious. Mysore onion dosa feels rich in flavour and is prepared in pure ghee. Kanchipuram idli was a decent one and a bit sour. Paniyaram was a one-of-a-kind and is a must try. Cheese pav bhaji was not bad but failed to meet the bar raised by other food items. For desserts, you have to have the pineapple sheera and you can thank me later. A south indian cuisines is incomplete with the iconic filter coffee and the coffee here will not disappoint you. The service is super quick and they serve you unlimited Sambar and Chutney

This restaurant was hitting home-runs after home-runs and I was about to give this place the coveted 5-star rating when they committed a hygienic blunder. I found a small hair in their Pav. Hygiene is as important as the taste and had they not compromised on the hygiene, my search for the 5-starred restaurant would have ended today. But alas the search continues!!

featured_reviews.name: Kaushik Kulkarni
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best south indian places to have breakfast/ lunch in Matunga. The ambience is pleasant and so is food. Menu is wide and many options are available for breakfast. South Indian thali is available for lunch. But overall I think the place is bit pricey.

Aaswad Upahaar & Mithaigrih, Dadar is conveniently located in the heart of Dadar at L.J. Road, Adjacent to Shivsena Bhavan. Since 1986, Aaswad has been a home to sumptuous Maharashtrian delicacies. It was also awarded Foodie Hub, UK Award for its Misal.

We also cater to large groups, accept party orders.
Do watch our space on social media for Festive Event Updates like Dhundur Maas, Sankrant Special, etc.

featured_reviews.name: Kaustubh Havanur
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best places for pure vegetarian food. This place is easily accessible as it is located right on the main road near Sena Bhavan. You can get down at Dadar Metro Station, and as soon as you come onto the main road, the restaurant is right beside it.

Whenever you visit, you will almost always find a rush here. The waiting time can range from 30 minutes to even 1 hour. However, they have now expanded their seating capacity, and there is also a lift available to reach the first floor.

The place is also very reasonably priced. We were a group of four friends and ordered around 7–8 items, yet the total bill was only around ₹1200.

You will find a wide variety of Maharashtrian dishes here, and they have also started serving some South Indian snacks.

Must try: Modak, Aamras, and Misal Pav
You can also try the Batata Vada.

Overall, it is a great place for pure vegetarian food and definitely worth visiting with friends and family.

featured_reviews.name: Vignesh
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best places for authentic Maharashtrian cuisine with exceptional flavors. We tried the thali, thalipeeth, vada pav, and kurma puri, and every dish was perfectly prepared—well-balanced, flavorful, and needing nothing extra. It’s easy to see why this place is already so popular in Dadar. The only drawback is the compact seating arrangement. Also, be prepared for a waiting time of around 15–30 minutes during peak hours or on busy days.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Aaswad Uphar Gruh & Mithai recently and had a proper Maharashtrian भोजन experience.
We tried a variety of items including Puri Bhaji, Seasonal Thali, Puran Poli, Lime Juice, Buttermilk, Kothimbir Vadi, and other traditional dishes. The food overall had that authentic, homely Maharashtrian taste which Aaswad is known for.
👉 Taste:
Most dishes were flavorful and well-prepared. The Puran Poli stood out – soft, perfectly sweet, and very satisfying. The Kothimbir Vadi was crispy and nicely spiced. The Seasonal Thali gave a good variety and felt wholesome.
👉 Quantity & Quality:
Portion sizes are decent, and ingredients taste fresh. It gives a proper “ghar jaisa khaana” vibe.
👉 Service & Waiting Time:
Had to wait around 40 minutes, which is quite long. The place gets very crowded, especially during peak hours.
👉 Ambience:
Simple, traditional setup. Nothing fancy, but clean and functional. Seating can feel a bit cramped during rush hours.

featured_reviews.name: Rushikesh Kale
featured_reviews.review_text: The best place to try authentic Maharashtrian food! The Misal Pav was amazing, and the Kothimbir Vadi was delicious. We also tried the Pola Usal, which was a real highlight. You must end your meal with the Piyush -it's so refreshing! Highly recommended, but be prepared to wait at least 30 minutes in the queue. It's worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja More
featured_reviews.review_text: Aaswad Uphar & Mithai Gruh at Shivaji Park is honestly one of the best places for Maharashtrian food. Their thalipith, misal pav and kothimbir vadi are always delicious and priced very reasonably. The food tastes authentic, the place is clean and hygienic, and you really get that homely Maharashtrian flavour. There’s almost always waiting outside, but trust me — the wait is totally worth it.👌👌

featured_reviews.name: sk 1
featured_reviews.review_text: Aaswad !! Heaven for Maharashtrian cusine lovers. Great experience and great food. Awesome Misal, Sabudana wada, Batata wada, Thalipeeth and more...to get a seat, we opted for a weekday and early dinner 😃

featured_reviews.name: Sarika Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prepared for a long wait, we were pleasantly surprised to find a table for two upon arrival. Being a week day may have also impacted numbers & wait times which otherwise apparently is a lot.
After a thorough scrutiny of the menu, we ordered pithla bhakri and a chaitra thali.
Pithla bhakri plate comes with two types of bhakris, rice & jowari.
The chaitra thali actually is good for two people which we realised when it arrived. Special mention of the jackfruit bhaaji, kajuchi usal and fresh unadulterated aamras with its natural sweetness & taste. The panah was too thick & sweet for my taste. Missed taking a pic of the thali.
My friend ordered puranpoli ice-cream for dessert & relished it. Again that is a huge portion with three scoops, too much for one person. See the pic :)
Definitely worth a visit to savour Maharashtrian cuisine in an iconic old eatery.
P.S. Five minutes walk from Dadar Aqualine metro station.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.

If you're a guac lover like me, you're in for a treat! We kicked things off with the Chilaquiles Filo Cups, and let me tell you-the guac was chef's kiss! The crispy, flaky texture of filo cups made every bite a delight.
Next up, the Mexican Tacodillas-creamy, with a simple yet satisfying filling.
For mains, the Genovese Pizza stole the show with its perfect crunch and just the right touch of caramelized brown onions. Then came the 2 Cheese Ravioli, generously topped with basil pesto sauce-because, let's be honest, cheese + pesto is always a winning combo!
One of our absolute faves? The Cottage Cheese Twists!🤤
The gravy was packed with flavor, and pairing it with sundried tomato olive roti? Game changer. 💯
They also have great cocktails & mocktails, trust the bartender's choice for it.
To wrap it all up, we indulged in the Lotus Biscoff Tea Cake with Coffee Ice Cream-an absolute must for coffee lovers ☕️ Rich, decadent, and a total devour-worthy dessert.

featured_reviews.name: Viraj Khedekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a weekend lunch at Millo. The restaurant is located in the Kamala Mills compound, so getting there is pretty easy.

The ambience is great. The restaurant is well maintained, clean and beautiful. The outdoor seating should probably be avoided during the monsoon. The tables are well spaced and the music is just the right volume so you don't need to shout to talk.
The service is quick and friendly. They will explain the menu and the contents of the dishes very well. They also accommodate dietary restrictions. They charge 10% as service fee.
The menu is fully vegetarian and expansive. They mainly cover Asian, Italian, and Mexican cuisines. We started with the comforting and tasty hot and sour mini soup. The Italian Tartine was tasty, the crostini were perfect to munch on. The Chilaquiles Filo Cups were a miss, the cups were nicely crisp but the guacamole was totally bland. The udon noodles were extremely tasty and were the second best item we tasted. Mind you, the noodles portion is large (for three, I'd guess). The kitchen seems to have nailed the Asian and Italian cuisine.

Overall, the experience was largely comforting. Definitely recommended, would revisit to taste more of the large menu.

They have a wide variety of chaats, North Indian snacks, sweets, and quick bites — most items are decent in quality and value for money. Service is fast, and this place continues to be a popular local landmark with a loyal fan following over the years.

featured_reviews.name: Umesh Rane
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mani’s Lunch Home-
Since 2007, during my monthly early morning office tours, I make it a personal ritual to stop at Mani’s Lunch Home in Matunga East for breakfast. No matter how early the day begins or how packed the schedule looks, I always get down here first—it’s my way of starting the day on the right note.
Over the years, I’ve tasted nearly every item served here. But my usual favorites are the idli-vada, medu vada, and the classic sada dosa. The idlis are soft and fluffy, the vadas crispy and golden, and the dosa—light, thin, and perfectly roasted. Each dish is accompanied by hot sambar and fresh coconut chutney that bring out authentic South Indian flavors.
One of the best parts of Mani’s is their warm and generous service. The staff pours unlimited sambar and chutney on your plate until you gently say “enough.” This simple yet heartfelt gesture has become the USP (Unique Selling Point) of the place. It's not just about the food, but the love and hospitality that comes with it.
Once I finish my meal, I always end with a cup of their aromatic filter coffee. Whether you prefer it light or strong, Mani’s coffee is brewed to perfection—rich, bold, and served in traditional steel tumblers that enhance its charm. For health-conscious guests like me, they also offer sugar-free tea, which is light, refreshing, and perfect to start the workday with clarity and balance.
After breakfast, I continue with my day feeling satisfied and refreshed. That peaceful moment at Mani’s sets a positive tone for whatever work lies ahead.
Mani’s Lunch Home is not just a restaurant for me. It’s a monthly ritual, a memory lane of flavors, and a place where time slows down—where every bite takes me back to the roots of comfort and tradition. In a fast-moving city like Mumbai, Mani’s is a calm, soulful corner that never changes.

featured_reviews.name: Ram Subramanian (Ram)
featured_reviews.review_text: Manis lunch home has always been my favorite spot from my college days in Matunga.On a Sunday I had some work in Matunga so decided to visit Manis lunch home . I am visiting this restaurant after a gap of 4 years. I ordered Idli vada sambar while my wife ordered lemon rice.The idli vada sambar was very good compared to all the ones I tasted in & around Mumbai. It was very close to the taste in southern part of India. In my college days visit to this restaurant made me nostalgic.As usual even after 24 years they still maintain the restaurant neat & clean. They still serve unlimited sambar & chutney with the dishes.I loved their chutney more than their sambar.The taste of idli vada was same as that tasted four year/ even 24 years before.It was always difficult to get a place to sit inside the restaurant during weekends especially the peak hours. Today we went at an odd time of 11 am so we could comfortably sit inside the small restaurant.The lemon rice was served with kerala pappadam & chutney. It tasted good. The rice looked bulky similar to that used in Kerala.Overall it tasted good.Then although my stomach was full I wanted to taste their plain dosa to which I am a bigger fan.The dosa taste amazing good & kudos to the team for maintaining their standards over the years. I topped it with a nice filter coffee. The coffee was great & a must have so whenever you have food here pls keep space for the filter coffee. My wife is a tea lover so she ordered Tea. The teas was good as per her. I did not want to spoil my coffee taste😜 so did not taste the tea.I love to keep the  taste of filter coffee to stay in my mouth as long as possible.It was nice to recollect old memories sitting in this restaurant. It had made our day.Thanks to the management to keep the restaurant intact even after so many years. Hats off to the team.It is a must visit restaurant in Mumbai if you like authentic South Indian breakfast.

featured_reviews.name: DNB Travel & Food Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
Classic South Indian Favourite with Great Food but Limited Parking

Review:
Cafe Mysore is one of Matunga’s iconic South Indian eateries — an institution famed for its authentic idlis, dosas, rasam vada, and filter coffee that have been delighting locals and food lovers for generations. The food is fresh, hearty, and very reasonably priced, making it a go-to breakfast or lunch spot for both regulars and first-timers. The dosa varieties (especially Dilkhush, Mysore masala) and pineapple sheera are often recommended by customers.

The ambience is casual and simple — not fancy, but clean and welcoming. It’s often busy during peak times (especially weekends and mornings), so be prepared for a bit of a crowd and sharing tables, which contributes to its classic local charm.

What We Loved 👍
Authentic South Indian flavours with generous portions.

Quick service most of the time for breakfast and tiffin items.

Pocket-friendly pricing.

Good for family breakfasts and casual meets.

Seating and comfort are basic; the place fills up quickly during rush hours.

Parking & Access 🚗
There is no dedicated parking lot or valet service at the cafe itself.

Being right on Matunga’s King’s Circle area, finding street parking can be challenging, especially during peak morning and evening hours. You may need to park in nearby public parking areas or use paid parking zones near the circle and walk a short distance.

If driving isn’t convenient, the cafe is very well connected by local transport, with King’s Circle railway station just a short walk away.

Best For: Authentic South Indian breakfast/lunch, quick meals, family outings, casual meet-ups.

Really enjoyed our meal at Shenoy’s. The food consistently delivers on quality and authenticity.

We had the Rassa Chicken, Prawns Ghee Roast with bhakri, and fried bombil as a starter. My dining partner ordered the Konkan thali, which was excellent. Their Ghee Roast preparations are the best I have had in Mumbai ( though it is a close call) and their Rassa Chicken has the potential to become my new Butter Chicken. The Fried Bombil is a new improved version - crispier than before and serious contender to be the best fried Bombil in Bombay.

Service was attentive without being intrusive. Naeem was switched on, friendly, and made all the right suggestions.

What stands out is the care in the cooking, you can genuinely taste the authenticity and effort in every dish. Shenoy’s has become one of those rare places that sets a benchmark for Konkan food. I see myself becoming a regular. Highly recommended for anyone interested in the cuisine.

The place is spacious, with a comfortable seating arrangement and classy décor that creates a pleasant ambiance. Since we were there early, we opted for idli, puri bhaji, a sandwich, and tea. The food was tasty, and I was impressed by how clean and well-maintained the restaurant was. I'll definitely return someday to try more of their offerings for lunch or dinner.

featured_reviews.name: George Grace
featured_reviews.review_text: Food is great. But what really spoils the overall experience is the slow service. Waiters don't come and ask if you need anything else unless you call them. And that in itself is a task since they keep running around and don't pay attention to the tables. One of the key reasons for visiting a restaurant is the service. If I need to ask for spoons and wait for spoons to arrive for a few mins after my food is delivered, then it doesn't make sense cause the food will already be cold by then.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Yeole
featured_reviews.review_text: Just wanted to share my experience about Benne Dosa. We have tried Benne Dosa and it was a complete disappointment.  The worst Benne Dosa i ever had ! Nor it was crispy no podi no salt nothing totally bland and no masala in it. Moreover when we informed the waiter he was laughing and turned his back to us. Utter disappointment. I suggest restaurant owner to please taste this dosa and do the changes also please ask the staff to be responsive. I will rate 0/5 for this Benne dosa that too very highly priced.

featured_reviews.name: J G Irani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food and friends make the best memories. So true! These are created at Dadar Darbar.
Dadar Darbar the most happening food and beverage restaurant set in a train dining car right outside Dadar East Station is a must visit for Mumbaikars and people travelling to Mumbai. Dadar Darbar is an affordable value for money, no frills, full on service, conveniently located restaurant. Dadar Darbar serves you North Indian menu with a twist. They create and cook up a fusion of indian, regional and international tastes for different palates.
For starters we had kheema paav, chicken lollypop, surmai fry, chicken spring roll. Whereas Hyderabadi chicken biryani was fulfilling as the main dish. For deserts we had Afghani dryfruits ice cream, Caramel custard and the Arabic pudding.
At Dadar Darbar, good food creates good mood!

featured_reviews.name: viraj s wadkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Darbar is a lifesaver for late-night travelers! The best part is that it’s open the whole night, so if you miss your last local train, this place feels like a cozy train compartment just a few steps from the station – literally next door!

The restaurant maintains good hygiene, which is a big plus, and the staff is polite. Service can be a little slow when it’s crowded, but that’s understandable. The food taste really surprised me – much better than expected!

If you’ve had a long train journey and need good food without traveling any further, this is the perfect spot. Convenient, clean, and satisfying late-night cravings right near the station!

featured_reviews.name: Huzefa Rangwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s a nice theme to have a restaurant in an old train compartment. Gives a different feel. Apart from the looks the food is actually good. It really tastes good. It’s not a fine dine restaurant so don’t expect amazing service but it was a good experience.
Since it is just outside the station, it is convenient if you have just arrived and are hungry. It’s affordable too, not too expensive.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Gaikwad.
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Darbar in Dadar East has become one of our go to places, and for good reason. We’ve visited many times, and the experience has consistently been wonderful. The food is genuinely delicious, rich in flavor, well prepared, and always satisfying. Whether it’s a quick meal or a relaxed outing, the quality never disappoints. What truly makes the place stand out is the service. The staff is polite, attentive, and always ready to help with a smile. A special mention goes to Mr. Irshad, who has attended our table on multiple occasions. His service is exceptional courteous, prompt, and very thoughtful. He makes sure everything is just right, which adds a personal touch to the entire dining experience.
The ambiance is comfortable and welcoming, making it a great spot for family visits as well as casual dining. Overall, Dadar Darbar offers a perfect combination of tasty food, great service, and a friendly atmosphere. We always look forward to coming back and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a satisfying meal in Dadar East.
